{{Short description|Painting made by filling numbers provided on the canvas}}
{{redirect|Color by numbers||Colour by Numbers (disambiguation)|and|Paint by number (disambiguation)}}
{{wiktionary|paint-by-numbers}}
[[File:Картины по номерам.jpg|thumb|A paint-by-number kit]]
'''Paint by number''' or '''painting by numbers''' kits are self-contained painting sets, designed to facilitate painting a pre-designed image. They generally include [[Paintbrush|brushes]], tubs of paint with numbered labels, and a [[Canvas#For painting|canvas]] printed with borders and numbers. The user selects the color corresponding to one of the numbers then uses it to fill in a delineated section of the canvas, in a manner similar to a [[coloring book]].

The kits were invented and developed in the late-1940s and 1950s by Max S. Klein, an engineer and owner of the Palmer Paint Company in Detroit, Michigan, United States, and Dan Robbins, a commercial artist.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-04-05 |title=Artist behind paint-by-numbers picture phenomenon dead at 93 |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/dan-robbins-artist-behind-paint-numbers-pictures-dead-93-n991226 |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2019-04-09 |title=Honoring The Creative Kitsch Of Paint-By-Numbers {{!}} KQED |url=https://www.kqed.org/pop/110874/honoring-the-creative-kitsch-of-paint-by-numbers |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=www.kqed.org |language=en}}</ref> 

When Palmer Paint introduced crayons to consumers, they also posted images online for a "Crayon by Number" version. In 1955 alone, Americans purchased more than $20 million worth of paint by number kits.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-04-04 |title=Dan Robbins: Paint-by-numbers inventor dies at 93 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-47822227 |access-date=2026-07-10 |language=en-GB}}</ref> The therapeutic benefits of paint by number kits have been widely reported.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-04-05 |title='Painting-by-numbers literally saved my life' |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/in-pictures-47832466 |access-date=2026-07-10 |language=en-GB}}</ref>
[[File:PaintByNumbers.jpg|thumb|A completed paint-by-number painting]]

== History ==
The first patent for the paint-by-number technique was filed in 1923.<ref name="nyTimesRobbinsObit">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/05/obituaries/dan-robbins-dead.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190406105604/https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/05/obituaries/dan-robbins-dead.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 6, 2019|title=Dan Robbins, Who Made Painting as Easy as 1-2-3 (and 4-5-6), Dies at 93|first=Katharine Q.|last=Seelye|date=April 5, 2019|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=April 6, 2019}} </ref> Paint by Number in its popular form was created by the Palmer Show Card Paint Company. The owner of the company approached employee Dan Robbins with the idea for the project. After several iterations of the product, the company in 1951 introduced the Craft Master brand, which went on to sell over 12 million kits.<ref name="nyTimesRobbinsObit"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/obituaries/dan-robbins-paint-by-number-inventor-who-made-every-man-a-rembrandt-dies-at-93/2019/04/05/6f80f412-574e-11e9-8ef3-fbd41a2ce4d5_story.html|title=Dan Robbins, paint-by-number inventor who made 'every man a Rembrandt,' dies at 93|first=Emily |last=Langer|newspaper=Washington Post}}</ref> This public response induced other companies to produce their own versions of painting by number. The Craft Master paint kit box tops proclaimed, "A BEAUTIFUL OIL PAINTING THE FIRST TIME YOU TRY."

Following the death of Max Klein in 1993, his daughter Jacquelyn Schiffman donated the Palmer Paint Co. archives to the [[National Museum of American History|Smithsonian Museum of American History]].<ref name=SI>{{cite web|url=https://americanhistory.si.edu/paint/rembrandt.html|title=PAINT BY NUMBERS|author=|date=|website=AmericanHistory.SI.edu|access-date=April 6, 2019}}</ref> The archival materials have been placed in the museum's Archives Center where they have been designated collection #544, the "Paint by Number Collection".

In 1992, [[Michael O'Donoghue]] and Trey Speegle organized and mounted a show of O'Donoghue's paint-by-number collection in New York City at the Bridgewater/Lustberg Gallery. After O'Donoghue's death, the [[Smithsonian Institution]]'s [[National Museum of American History]] exhibited many key pieces from O'Donoghue's collection, now owned by Speegle, along with works from other collectors in 2001.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=SI/>

In 2008, a private collector in Massachusetts assembled over 6,000 paint-by-number works dating back to the 1950s from eBay and other American collectors to create the Paint By Number Museum, a registered [[501(c)(3) organization|501(c)(3)]] non-profit organization which has become the world's largest online archive of paint-by-number works. The private collector's identity has remained an open question and subject of speculation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paint By Numbers Generator |url=https://paintbynumbers.net/ |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=PaintbyNumbers.NET |language=en|last=Andy|first=Tsu}}</ref> In 2011, the [[Museum of Modern Art]] in New York accepted four early designs of paint by number by Max S. Klein for its Department of Architecture and Design, donated by Jacquelyn Schiffman.<ref>{{Cite web |last=kueber |first=pam |title=What to collect: Paint By Number paintings - A comprehensive online guide |url=https://retrorenovation.com/2012/07/18/what-to-collect-vintage-paint-by-number-paintings/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=Retro Renovation |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2026, [[London Zoo]] celebrated their 200 year anniversary by organising the largest paint by number of all time, with 14,000 people participating.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ZSL achieves Guinness World Records title with record-breaking artwork {{!}} London Zoo |url=https://www.londonzoo.org/zoo-stories/news/zsl-achieves-guinness-world-records-title-record-breaking-artwork |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=www.londonzoo.org |language=en}}</ref>
